Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and ask so we can move to an eval-ready artifact: 

Recap (short)
- Primary goal: surface a high-precision Q&A assistant over your internal docs and support tickets with <100ms median token latency for short responses.
- Priority metrics: F1 on labeled answers, hallucination rate on a 500-sample test set, and customer satisfaction delta on triaged support cases.
- Production constraints: PII redaction is required (GDPR + customer contract), and anything that looks like PHI must be blocked.

Recommended next steps for the eval pack (what we need from you)
1) Customer query bank: 500–1,000 examples representative of full-support traffic. Prefer CSV with columns: id, user_text, intent_label (if available), priority, and whether the example contains sensitive data.
2) Edge-case buckets: a brief list of ~8 categories you worry about (legal text, invoice numbers, code snippets, long lists, mixed-language, customer-specific identifiers).
3) Redaction preferences: what to mask vs. what to preserve for context (examples welcome).
4) Benchmarks & tooling: we will run a 3-model sweep (13B dense, 7B quantized, and a tuned instruction-tuned 3B) with scoring on correctness/hallucination/latency.

Attachments & links:
- I’ll upload a short redaction checklist and our suggested CSV template — see drive link after I set permissions.

Can you send an initial batch (50–100 rows) this week so we can start the intake and give quick feedback on redaction before you send the full set?

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min screen share if that helps with formatting.

Mina — ran the sample through our intake script and the quick findings are below. Attached is a redaction playbook draft and a cleaned 55-row CSV (we removed 5 rows with explicit SSNs and replaced tokens with <REDACTED_ID>).

Quick findings:
- Regex coverage: SSN/CC numbers caught in 98% of cases; free-text addresses are spotty and need heuristics.
- False positives: invoice numbers in format INV-2028-XXX were sometimes treated as CC-like numeric sequences; flagged and preserved where pattern matched.
- Hallucination risk: long technical support logs with stack traces cause the model to invent root causes if not truncated or summarized.

Redaction playbook (high level)
- Always mask: SSN, full credit card numbers, full passport numbers, customer PII (emails when not explicitly allowed).
- Context-preserve: customer IDs (CUST-XXXX) can be replaced with stable tokens; preserve relative ordering.
- Summarize long attachments: if a message references an attachment >20KB, replace body with "[ATTACHMENT_SUMMARY_REQUIRED]" and request upload through secure share.

Next steps
1) Elena: confirm you can accept the 55-row cleaned CSV and review the playbook.
2) Mina: once Elena signs off, we’ll run the 3-model sweep and share the initial benchmark (expected 48 hours).
3) Marissa: can you prepare the eval rubric template (accuracy, hallucination, latency, safety) and drop it into the drive link?

Attachments: redaction_playbook_v1.pdf, cleaned_customer_queries_sample.csv

Thanks —
